title: 3 Beginner Mistakes with Index Funds
audience: Nervous beginner investors anywhere in the world.
brief: Warm, encouraging tone for nervous beginners. Explain what an index fund is and the beginner mistakes to avoid. Goal: viewers join the free email course at moneybasics.example/course.

issues.description: The title and opening promise three mistakes, but only two are covered; the closing wraps up without a third mistake.
Claims index funds beat 90 percent of professional fund managers 'every single year', an absolute statement with no source; the real figure varies by year and period.

Guarantees the viewer will double their money in five years, says they 'can't lose', and tells them to put emergency savings into the fund: a guaranteed-returns financial claim and unsafe personal advice.
Tells a worldwide audience to open a Roth IRA or 401(k) at Fidelity or Vanguard, which exist only in the United States.
A condescending outburst ('what are you even doing?', 'grown adults') contradicts the brief's warm, encouraging tone for nervous beginners.

lines.text: If you have ever wondered whether you are too late, too young, or too clueless to start investing, this video is for you.
Today I am sharing the three biggest mistakes beginners make with index funds, and how to avoid every one of them.
First, what is an index fund?
It is a single fund that holds a small piece of many companies at once, so you are spreading your money across hundreds of businesses instead of betting on just one.
To get started, just open a Roth IRA or a 401(k) through Fidelity or Vanguard, and pick an S and P five hundred fund.
That's it.
Mistake number one: waiting for the perfect moment.
Nobody can time the market, and time in the market usually matters more than timing.
Starting small and early beats starting big and late.
Index funds beat ninety percent of professional fund managers every single year, so there is really no reason to ever pay for active management.
Mistake number two: panic selling.
Markets fall sometimes, and that is normal.
The people who get hurt are usually the ones who sell during the drop and lock in the loss.
And honestly, if you don't already know that, what are you even doing?
It is the most basic thing in investing, and I cannot believe I have to explain it to grown adults.
Here is my promise to you.
I guarantee that if you put your emergency savings into an index fund today, you will double your money in five years.
You literally cannot lose.
So those are the mistakes to avoid. Start early, and don't panic.
Index funds are a simple tool, and that is all there is to it.
If you want the full beginner roadmap, join the free email course at moneybasics dot example slash course.
See you next time.
